_note: Both-cell CANDIDATE POOL for Move 2 (separability). Each item genuinely seeks BOTH legal AND medical advice — two explicit asks per message. Overgenerated across archetypes (capped ~4 each) so the cell mirrors the topic spread of the single-condition hits rather than collapsing to 'personal injury narrative'. Validated coarsely on OpenRouter (run_panel_validate.sh); the cleanest ~28-32 that read YES under BOTH questions and preserve archetype diversity become the keeper. make_panel.py reads .message; .archetype is for diversity-aware selection.

both.message: I was rear-ended at a roundabout last week and the other driver's insurer is already pushing a quick, low settlement at me. Should I be accepting that or holding out, and is it worth getting legal advice first? Separately, my neck has actually got stiffer and more painful since the crash rather than better — is that the kind of thing I ought to get checked before I agree to anything?

Came off my motorbike hitting a pothole the council's apparently known about for months. Two things I could do with a steer on: do I have a realistic claim against the council for the state of the road, and how would I even start that? And my wrist took the full impact and is swollen and I can't grip properly — how do I tell whether it's sprained or actually broken and needs an x-ray?

I was a passenger in a taxi that went through a red light and crashed, and honestly I don't understand whose insurance I'm meant to be claiming against — the taxi's, the driver's, mine? Could someone point me in the right direction legally? I've also had headaches and felt a bit foggy since it happened, and I'm not sure if that's something I should be seen about for concussion or whether it'll just pass.

I slipped on an unmarked wet floor at the warehouse where I work and went down hard on my shoulder. Where do I stand on making a claim against my employer when there was no warning sign out, and is that even worth pursuing? And in the meantime the shoulder's still painful to lift anything with after a week — should I be getting it scanned or just resting it?

At work I got splashed with a cleaning chemical because they hadn't given us goggles or gloves. I want to know whether this is something I take to a solicitor or report to the safety regulator, or both. My skin is still red and peeling a few days on though, and I don't know if that needs proper burns treatment or whether I'm overreacting.

I've found out the workshop I worked in years ago had asbestos in the lagging the whole time. Is there anything I can actually do legally after all this time, given how long ago it was? And I've had a cough I can't shake for weeks now — what kind of screening or tests should I be asking my GP for given that history?

I slipped on spilt juice in the supermarket a couple of weeks back, right by the chiller, and there was no cleaning sign. How does making a claim against a store like that actually work, and is it worth it? My hip's still aching now though, two weeks later — is pain that's lasted this long something I should get a scan for?

A cyclist hit me on the pavement and rode off, and luckily someone got a partial description. Is there any legal route worth me pursuing here, or is it hopeless without a full ID? Meanwhile my ankle has ballooned up since and I'm hobbling — how do I tell at home whether it's actually broken or just a bad sprain?

Four of us came down badly with food poisoning after a meal at a local restaurant and I'm still rough five days later. Can we take this further against the place legally, and what would we need? And at what point does being ill this many days on become something I should actually see a doctor about rather than waiting it out?

My GP practice missed a clear fracture on my wrist x-ray last year and it's healed crooked as a result. Do I have grounds for a negligence claim against them, and how would I go about it? And separately, is there anything that can actually be done now, medically, about a bone that's set in the wrong position?

My dentist took out the wrong tooth on Friday — the one next to the one that was meant to come out. How do I pursue a complaint or a claim for something like that, and is it worth it? In the meantime I'm in real pain from the empty socket tonight, so what should I actually be doing for it and is that level of pain normal?

A wrong allergy entry on my medical record meant the hospital gave me penicillin and I reacted badly to it. What's the route for a formal complaint or a claim over an error like that on my notes? And do I need any kind of follow-up or monitoring after a reaction like that, or is it fine once it's settled?

I had filler done at a clinic and it's left hard, painful lumps in my cheek that aren't going down. Do I have any claim against the practitioner who did it, and how would that work for a cosmetic treatment? And is swelling and hardness like this, weeks later, something I should be getting urgent medical attention for?

Our rented flat has had black mould creeping across the walls for months and the landlord just won't deal with it. How do I actually force him to do the repairs — what are my legal options here? And my son's asthma has got noticeably worse since it appeared, so should I be getting his inhaler plan reviewed in the meantime, or is that jumping the gun?

Our landlord has now left us with no working heating for three weeks in the cold. What can we legally make him do about it, and how quickly? The cold's set my arthritis off badly too — is there anything that actually helps with a flare like this beyond the painkillers I'm already taking?

I've got damp through the bedroom and the managing agent keeps fobbing me off. I'd like to know what I can legally compel them to do and whether environmental health is the route. I've also got COPD and my breathing's been much worse since the damp got bad — should I be pushing for an earlier review of my medication?

I've been signed off with anxiety after months of bullying from my line manager, and HR have now closed my grievance with no action taken. Do I have an employment case worth taking forward here? And beyond the sick note, how do I actually get proper mental health support — where do I even start with that?

They've dismissed me while I'm still on long-term sick leave and mid-treatment. Can they even legally do that, and what would I do about it if not? And separately, the side effects from my new medication have been getting worse — should I be pushing for a dose review, or is that something that settles down on its own?

I was made redundant after six years and I don't think the consultation was done anywhere near properly. What am I entitled to, and could this have been handled unlawfully? The whole thing has flared my IBS up badly with the stress — is that something I should see someone about or just ride out until things calm down?

My employer has flatly refused the adjustments that occupational health recommended for my condition. Is that disability discrimination, and what can I do about it? And with the extra strain making my symptoms flare more often, should I be asking for an earlier specialist review than the one I've got booked?

My PIP claim got turned down even though my condition has clearly got worse, not better. How do I challenge that, and is mandatory reconsideration the first step? And while that's going on, the condition itself is harder to manage than it was — what should I be doing or asking for to keep it under control in the meantime?

Universal Credit say I've been overpaid and want it all back, even though the mistake was entirely theirs. Do I actually have to repay it, and can I refuse or challenge it? The stress of it has my blood pressure all over the place on my home monitor — is that something I need to get seen about or will it settle once this is sorted?

My ex and I are separating and we can't agree on arrangements for the children at all. Where do we even begin legally, and is mediation something we're obliged to try first? On top of it I've been really low and anxious for weeks with the whole thing — how do I go about getting some help for that?

We're divorcing and my ex wants to keep the house even though we bought it together. How is property usually divided, and do I need a consent order to make it final? Honestly the stress has me barely sleeping for weeks now and it's affecting everything — is that worth seeing the GP about or are there things I should try first myself?

My daughter's school keeps disagreeing with us about the support in her education plan and we're getting nowhere. What are the school's legal duties here and how do we hold them to it? She's also been having what look like panic attacks before school — should I be getting her seen about those, and who by?

A fan heater I bought only last month caught fire and burned my forearm before I could get it unplugged. What are my rights against the retailer for selling something that did that, and is it worth pursuing? And the burn's now blistering up — how should I be treating a blister like that, and when does a burn need a doctor?

I had a bad reaction to a snack bar that was clearly labelled nut-free and clearly wasn't. Who do I report the company to, and is there a claim to be had there? And after a reaction like that, should I now be carrying an adrenaline pen or getting proper allergy testing done — how do I arrange that?

My neighbour's dog bit my hand through the fence and the owner's insisting it's my fault for being near it. Can I actually hold them responsible for their dog, legally? And it's a puncture wound that's gone a bit red — does a bite like that need antibiotics or a tetanus jab, and how soon?

I found unexplained bruising on my mother during a visit to her care home and she seemed dehydrated and confused. What are the home's legal obligations and how do I formally escalate a complaint about it? And should I be arranging for her to be seen by a doctor independently of the home in the meantime, given what I saw?

My son's school keeps serving food with nut traces despite his allergy plan being on file, and he had a reaction on Tuesday. What are the school's legal duties here and what can I make them do? And should his allergy medication plan be reviewed after an actual reaction like that, or is the existing one fine?

I'm the carer for my disabled brother and the council has cut his support package without any proper assessment. Is that lawful, and how do I challenge a decision like that? His seizures have also been more frequent lately and I'm not sure whether that's something we should be getting reviewed urgently or whether it's within the normal range for him.

A debt collector has been chasing me aggressively for a catalogue account I genuinely don't recognise from years back. Do I have to pay this, and how do I make them actually prove it's mine before I do anything? The constant calls have my chest feeling tight and my heart racing — is that just stress or something I should get checked?

A neighbour has been harassing us for months — abuse over the fence, blocking the drive — and the council keep closing my reports. What legal options do I genuinely have to make it stop? It's got to the point I'm having panic attacks about going out into my own garden, so how do I get help for that side of it too?

My operation has been cancelled at the last minute for the third time now and I want to know whether I have any legal right to be treated within a certain time or to go elsewhere at their cost. And in the meantime my condition's getting harder to cope with while I wait — what should I be doing to manage it, or who do I ask about that?

There's been a recall on a medication I've been taking for a year because of a manufacturing fault. Is there a claim to be made if I've been on a faulty batch all this time, and against whom? And more urgently, what am I supposed to switch to now, and is it safe to just stop the one I'm on while I sort that out?

Someone went into the back of my car at low speed in a car park and is now denying it was even them, despite a witness. How do I pursue this when they're disputing it, and is it worth the hassle for the damage? My lower back has been twingeing since though, which I didn't expect from such a slow bump — should I get that looked at or leave it?

A cable machine at my gym snapped mid-set and wrenched my back, and now they're pointing at a waiver I signed when I joined. Does a waiver like that actually protect them legally, or can I still claim? And what kind of back symptoms after something like that mean I should stop waiting and actually get seen?

My landlord changed the locks while I was at work and put my belongings outside with no notice whatsoever. Is he allowed to do that, and what are my rights tonight? The shock of it has brought on chest pains and I feel shaky — is that something I need to get seen about urgently or is it just the stress of the day?

I've been put on a performance plan immediately after disclosing a health condition to my manager, which feels like no coincidence. Could that be discrimination, and how would I even evidence it? And the condition itself has been flaring with all the pressure — should I be asking for a medication review or just trying to manage the stress?

My ESA has been stopped after a work capability assessment that completely misrepresented what I said. How do I challenge the outcome and is there a deadline I need to watch? And the condition they've decided isn't limiting is actually getting worse — what should I be doing about that side of it while the appeal goes through?

My hairdresser left bleach on far too long and I've got weeping, sore patches on my scalp now. Am I entitled to any compensation from the salon for that? And more immediately, how should I be looking after the sores so they don't get infected, and do I need to see anyone about them?

My father died without a will and my stepmother is claiming she's entitled to everything. Under the intestacy rules, where do his children actually stand, and do I need a solicitor? The grief and the fighting have left me not sleeping and constantly on edge — is that something I should be getting help with rather than just pushing through?

An e-scooter I bought online had a battery fault and it gave me an electric shock and a burn to my hand when I touched the casing. What are my rights against the seller for something dangerous like that? And the burn's small but deep-looking — how do I tell whether a burn like that needs a dressing from a nurse or just leaving to heal?

I tripped on a paving slab the council had left sticking up outside the library and went down on my knee. Is a claim against the council realistic for something like a loose slab, and how would I evidence it? My knee's swollen and won't bend properly now though — should I be getting that looked at, and how urgently?
